templates.header: Duration: {duration} minutes. Starting checkpoint: {prev_tag}. Ending checkpoint: {tag} ({hash}).
templates.access_before: Give your coding agent access to the supplied incident-platform.zip or the reference repository in the
templates.access_after: . Ask it to preserve the embedded checkpoint history and identify the learner project separately from the reference.
templates.agent_role: Your coding agent handles preparation, implementation and execution. You set the scope, inspect its changes and explain the evidence. This development assistant is separate from the investigation agents inside the platform.
templates.prepare_prompt: Prepare my Python learner project for Lesson {nn}, starting from {prev_tag}. Locate the supplied reference repository and my existing work; ask for their locations if needed. Preserve my changes and handle repository setup, dependency installation and environment configuration yourself. Use the pinned Python 3.12 environment and offline mock provider. Establish the starting checkpoint without adding this lesson yet. Run the baseline checks and report the workspace, checkpoint, results and any missing prerequisites. Do not ask me to run terminal commands.
templates.orient_intro: Next, orient the coding agent to the reference while preserving your work.
templates.orient_prompt: Compare my current project with {prev_tag} and prepare a read-only view of {tag} for this lesson. Preserve my work while arranging any isolation needed. Identify differences, relevant files and the expected capability. Explain the implementation sequence before we begin; do not replace my project with the finished reference or add later lessons.
templates.readiness: Have your coding agent rehearse the completed reference and prepare the current tests, fixtures and lab runner before class. Tests may fail until the capability is implemented. During class, use one bounded prompt at a time; learners inspect the change, explain the control decision and review the check evidence.
templates.offline: Have the coding agent use the offline mock provider for class. If live access fails, restore that configuration and continue. Keep credentials in secure configuration. Adapter request shapes were tested with mock HTTP; live account access was not exercised.
templates.pinned: Pinned versions in pyproject.toml and uv.lock: Python 3.12, MCP 2.2.0, A2A SDK 1.1.2, httpx 0.28.1, FastAPI 0.141.1, uvicorn 0.52.4, jsonschema 4.26.0, pytest 9.1.1 and pytest-asyncio 1.4.0. Have the coding agent manage their installation.
templates.script_intro: Use SAY for instructor narration, SHOW and REVIEW for the code and evidence participants examine, PROMPT for text they give their coding agents, and PAUSE for discussion. Prompts define scope and expected behaviour; the agent handles command execution. Code excerpts remain as reading and review material from the exact reference checkpoint, not manual typing instructions.
templates.opening_show: The coding agent’s baseline report, current learner project, synthetic incident records and lesson outcome. Ask participants to explain what already works before authorizing the next bounded change.
templates.concept_pause: Invite one learner to trace the control flow and another to identify a failure boundary. Resolve different interpretations before opening the implementation.
templates.step_show: The current learner implementation and {file}. Use the following prompt to make the bounded change, then inspect the agent’s result.
templates.step_prompt: For Lesson {nn}, continue in my learner project. {body} Use {tag} read-only to check compatibility. Preserve earlier behaviour, run relevant checks and show the change and observed evidence. Stop at this step.
templates.review: Compare the coding agent’s change with this reference excerpt. It covers source lines {start} to {end} at {tag}; common indentation is reduced for display. Ask the agent to explain material differences in behaviour.
templates.step_pause: Have learners identify the boundary in their agent’s change and explain the expected failure behaviour. Compare it with the reference snapshot before accepting the change.
templates.exercise_prompt: Help me carry out the Lesson {nn} learner exercise in my existing project: {body} First state the expected outcomes, then run the experiment in a recoverable state. Show the observed results and explain any discrepancy. Keep the original acceptance criteria and restore temporary experiments when finished.
templates.verify: Give the coding agent the verification prompt below, then inspect its evidence and explain the result in your own words.
templates.verify_prompt: Verify my Lesson {nn} implementation against its completion criteria. Update the checkpoint indicator in incident/__init__.py to {n} only when the required capability is present. Run tests/test_lesson{nn}.py, the Session {nn} demonstration and the existing regression suite using the offline provider. Keep the expected outcomes unchanged. Report checks actually executed, failures, relevant output and any untested integration. Explain the result and save a recoverable checkpoint of my work. Do not equate an unrun or skipped check with a pass.
templates.expected_behaviour: The coding agent returns actual check results and the demonstration’s structured output. Run identifiers and elapsed times vary. Compare the status and capability outcomes with the recorded reference below, and investigate differences.
templates.practice_pause: Ask learners to explain the evidence before accepting the checkpoint. If a check fails, use the specific recovery prompt below and review the resulting correction.
templates.recorded: The independently unpacked {tag} checkpoint passed its full test suite and this lesson demo. Recorded test result: {passed} passed in {seconds}s. Have your coding agent save a recoverable learner checkpoint and retain the comparison with {tag} ({hash}).
templates.files_intro: Use this inventory to scope the coding agent’s work. It includes core files, lab scaffolding, acceptance tests and checkpoint metadata. Ask the agent to explain any additional file changes it needs.
templates.review_prompt: Compare my completed Lesson {nn} work with reference {tag}. Show the changed files, interfaces and important behavioural differences. Explain how each completion criterion is met with code or test evidence. Preserve deliberate learner improvements and earlier capabilities; do not overwrite my work merely to obtain a textually identical copy.
templates.recovery_prompt: I am working on Lesson {nn}. The symptom is: {symptom} Diagnostic focus: {diagnostic} Recovery guidance: {recovery} Reproduce the issue, make the smallest necessary correction and rerun affected checks. Report the cause, changed files and observed outcome. Preserve security controls and acceptance criteria.
templates.discussion: Which decision would change for a larger or more sensitive workload, and what additional evidence would you require before changing it? Tie the answer to the code, the task requirements and the acceptance checks.

verification_scope.tested: All course tags were independently unpacked and tested. The completed repository has 51 passing tests. Real local MCP stdio, the tool gateway's shared sessions and pinned definitions, A2A HTTP discovery, streaming, delegated-token authentication and cancellation were exercised. The platform console was driven in a headless Chromium browser against every checkpoint from lesson-08 onward.
verification_scope.not_tested: Live model credentials, paid provider calls, live model judging, third-party MCP or A2A services, remote MCP OAuth, an enterprise identity provider, a managed secret vault, production cloud rollout and an external observability collector were not tested. The offline provider is a deterministic fixture, so its usage and quality results are teaching measurements. Read TESTING.md for the full scope and environment details.
verification_scope.local_effects: The SQLite mock-effect ledger proves its local transaction boundary. It does not guarantee exactly-once effects for arbitrary external APIs. The A2A specialist task store is in memory. The restricted Compose sandbox uses temporary writable state; persistent deployment storage requires separate configuration and validation.
verification_scope.platform_identity: Tokens are HMAC-signed with one shared development key so the course runs offline; a production issuer signs asymmetrically and publishes verification keys. The credential store keeps values in process memory and is not a vault. The gateway runs in the platform process; production gateways are usually separate network services.

learner_prompts.title: Coding agent prompts for the course
intro: Give your coding agent access to the reference repository and your learner project. Use the current prompts even when inspecting earlier code checkpoints. The agent handles environment setup, repository operations, execution and verification. You set scope, inspect code and decide whether the observed evidence meets the lesson criteria.

These prompts guide a learner implementation; a coding agent’s completion message is not proof that its result passed the checks. Use offline fixtures unless you deliberately configure and authorize a live integration.

platform_components: Agent runtime: bounded ReAct loop, typed run state, event log
Tool contracts, approval boundary and MCP transport
Context selection, retrieval, memory and versioned artifacts
Durable runs, crash recovery and exact-action approval
Supervisor, scoped subagents and parallel coordination
Platform core: agent registry, run API and platform console
MCP tool gateway: policy, audit and shared upstream sessions
Agent identity, delegated credentials and credential store
Operations: traces, admission control and evaluated releases
Tuning, before/after evidence and the capstone presentation
